properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shor-vulnerable curve, but its role is semantic compatibility: the precompile set mirrors what Ethereum/RISC-V guest programs compute, so replacement is a protocol-level decision, not a code change any one deployment can make. Changeable here only as an implementation detail.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Proof-system integrity checks on public data: keep as constant-time-compare hygiene (subtle crate) but not as an exploitable side channel — nothing secret is compared.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Classical NIST curve available to guest proofs; the canonical label ECDH-P256 overstates — the sites are curve-arithmetic precompiles, not a live ECDH session.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Classical signature verification inside proofs; mirrors ecosystem semantics (Ed25519 consensus rules), replaceable only by protocol decision.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two distinct roles: the TEE site is a host-side security control ("2FA" for the proving system); the zkvm-lib/patch-testing sites are guest-facing verify APIs. Classical signatures → ML-DSA-65 on the TEE path; the EVM paths are protocol-locked.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: curve25519-dalek library surface is real and pinned to sp1-patches forks; but judge it as Edwards/Ed25519 arithmetic, not as X25519 key agreement. The only ECDH-in-guest surface is the separate sp1-lib ecdh module (ALG-c9ffc8a8).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Guest-facing ECDH surface of the zkVM: proofs can contain classical ECDH computations. Host code has no ECDH call of its own.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak/SHA-3 is Grover-limited only (square-root speedup) — not Shor-vulnerable; it is also the recursion-friendly hash of the STARK. No migration pressure beyond CNSA-style digest-size policy.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Grover-limited symmetric hash; fine cryptographically. Note for coverage: the zkEVM's EIP-152 BLAKE2f precompile (zkevm/libzkevm/src/precompile/blake2f.rs) is a separate site not in this object — filed as its own finding.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Grover-limited; standard SHA-2. No PQ action beyond digest-size policy (CNSA prefers SHA-384).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Optional AWS-KMS signer for the SP1 prover network ("network" cargo feature, off by default). Custody is entirely in the AWS control plane — observable here, changeable only by AWS. The signing algorithm is fixed by whatever KMS key the ARN points at (alloy AwsSigner does Ethereum-style ECDSA, i.e. ECC_SECG_P256K1 keys).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared-dependency inventory: the algorithm surface ships in the build even without an in-repo call site; reachable at runtime through any dependency that links it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Platform TLS = classical ECDHE key exchange with no PQ groups; the transport posture of that workspace is whatever the host OpenSSL negotiates.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Go crypto surface available in the compiled verifier; the gnark BN254 Groth16/Plonk usage it accompanies is filed as its own finding.
